name: Z-Lock
description: A modern leg lock submission from single-leg X (SLX) or 50/50 that combines ankle lock pressure with heel hook rotation mechanics — attacking the opponent's knee and ankle simultaneously.
shortInstruction: From SLX, underhook the near leg, bring your outside leg over their thigh, trap their foot at your hip, rotate your hips to the mat — combined ankle and heel hook finish.
summary: The Z-lock is a hybrid leg lock submission that combines elements of the ankle lock and heel hook into a single devastating attack. Originating from positions like single-leg X (SLX) and 50/50 guard, it uses a unique leg configuration to trap and torque the opponent's leg. The position offers excellent control and can be used both as a finishing submission and as a transitional position to other leg attacks like the saddle or cross ashi garami. It is particularly effective in no-gi and modern leg lock systems.
whyItWorks: Combines two attack vectors (ankle + knee) simultaneously, creating a dilemma for the opponent — defending one exposes the other.
Uses hip rotation and body weight rather than just arm strength, making it mechanically efficient.
The foot trap at the hip prevents the opponent from rolling out or turning to escape.
Can be entered directly from common guard positions (SLX, 50/50) without complex re-positioning.
Creates extreme isolation of the knee joint by fixing the foot at the hip while rotating the torso.
commonMistakes: Losing the underhook on the near leg, allowing the opponent to free their leg and escape.
Failing to trap the foot securely at the hip before initiating rotation.
Using only upper body strength instead of engaging hip rotation for the finish.
Applying the submission too slowly, giving the opponent time to stack or roll.
Over-rotating and losing control of the trapped leg after the finish.
coachingCues: Trap the foot like you're pinning it to your hip bone — don't let it slide.
Rotate your hips to the mat, not your shoulders — power comes from the core.
Keep their heel tight against your body to maximize leverage.
Enter from SLX when they posture: underhook + leg over = Z-lock.
If they roll, follow their hip and re-attack — don't reset.
safetySummary: Z-lock applies rotational torque to the knee — tap early and respect the submission.
Not appropriate for beginners — requires solid leg lock understanding before attempting.
The combined ankle + knee pressure can cause injury to both joints if applied explosively.
Partners rolling should establish clear tapping protocols for leg attacks.
keyCorrections: If you can't finish, your foot trap is too loose — pull their foot tighter against your hip.
If they roll, follow their hip rotation — release the lock and re-attack from saddle.
If you feel resistance in their knee, release pressure — do not force the rotation.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: SLX or 50/50: underhook the near leg → bring outside leg over their thigh → trap their foot at your hip → rotate your hips toward the mat → finish.

decisionTree.action: The Z-lock chains with the saddle: if they roll to escape the Z-lock, enter the saddle.

moneyDetails: The underhook on their near leg must be deep — your arm should wrap around their thigh, not just the knee.
Your outside leg goes over their thigh and pins their leg against your body.
Trap their foot against your hip by keeping your knee tight to their body.
The finish comes from rotating your hips toward the mat while keeping their foot pinned — this combines ankle and knee pressure.
nextStep: After the Z-lock, learn the saddle/inside sankaku control and the inside heel hook.
fixItFast: Leg keeps slipping? Your underhook is too shallow — dig deeper on the thigh.
Can't finish? Your foot trap is loose — pull it tighter against your hip.
They roll? Follow their hips and enter the saddle — don't fight it.
